sourceIssues.reason: The cited survey theorem assumes a shrunken alcove. In split adjoint A2 take λ=ω2∨, x=s2s1, y=1. The published construction gives J=∅, J′={s1}, x′=s2, z=s1, γ=λ, y′=1 and a=s1s2. On the negative base alcove u<0, v<0, u+v>−1, w sends (u,v) to (v−1,1−u−v), with positive-root ranges (−2,−1),(1,2),(0,1). The seed a t^γ sends it to (1−u−v,u), whose second coordinate lies in the critical strip (−1,0). Both finite factors have full support. This disproves applicability of the cited theorem, not nonemptiness or the main result. The extraction’s stronger claim that every nonregular γ causes failure is false and is not retained.

sourceIssues.reason: Each simple-root pairing with 2ρ∨ is 2, so μ0 is dominant for large N and μ0+λ′−λ is in the nonnegative integral coroot cone. If μ≤_Zμ0 is dominant and μ0−μ=Σ n_iα_i∨, then Σ n_i=〈ρ,μ0−μ〉≤〈ρ,μ0〉; hence there are finitely many such μ. A minimal feasible element below μ0 exists, and lower-directedness makes it globally least. This is a routine completion, not a false theorem. The inherited proposed direction Σ(simple coroots) is wrong: in D4 its simple-root pairings are (1,−1,1,1). Input item /53 already uses the valid 2ρ∨ direction.

sourceIssues.reason: For split SL3, ω1∨=(2α1∨+α2∨)/3 is not a cocharacter, so the factor t^{ρ_J∨} with J={s1} is not in its Iwahori–Weyl group. The obstruction can persist in γ: in unramified simply connected ²A2, let σ exchange the nodes, λ=(3,3), x=1,y=s1 in fundamental-coweight coordinates. Then x′=s2 and γ=λ−ω1∨+s2ω2∨=(3,2), with coroot coordinates (8/3,7/3), whereas λ has integral coroot coordinates (3,3). Equality of auxiliary Kottwitz coinvariants does not produce a lift. GHN’s adjoint comparison is componentwise after its erratum. Its equal-characteristic geometric comparison has a coprimality hypothesis; p.652 separately supplies a mixed-characteristic set bijection without that hypothesis. The final dimension transfer needs its appropriate geometric or combinatorial justification. H14 §1.4 explicitly assumes adjoint type, unlike H21’s standing reduction. No counterexample to He21 Theorem 6.1 is claimed.

sourceIssues.locator: GHN15, P-alcoves and nonemptiness of affine Deligne–Lusztig varieties, Ann. Sci. ÉNS 48 (2015), Proposition 2.2.1, p.651.
sourceIssues.correction: Retain the componentwise flag isomorphisms. Assert a global immersion only with injectivity of the component-group map, and retain the characteristic hypothesis of the comparison.
sourceIssues.reason: The authors’ erratum, Proposition 0.0.1, removes automatic injectivity and gives the corrected componentwise statement. In equal characteristic the comparison assumes char(k) does not divide |π1(G_ad)|. Its subsequent description of the kernel by torsion in cocharacter coinvariants is stated for semisimple G, not arbitrary reductive G. The He21 adjoint reduction must import the corrected result, rather than the original global assertion. Independently, G=G_m has π0(Flag)=Z and trivial adjoint group, so its component map is not injective; the coprimality hypothesis holds because π1(G_ad)=0.
